quote: Do you have any, like, over the head, like, drone shots of your home by chance?
stewart_read: Rep spends significant time chasing a drone shot for a brand-new home instead of quickly pivoting to the standard roof-type/age question and moving on.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may be trying to get imagery for a more accurate design, which is a legitimate goal — but it derails the verify flow for over a minute.
coaching_implication: Ask roof type/age directly per script first; only chase drone shots as a follow-up capture item after verify is complete.

quote: I have five mini splits in the house.
stewart_read: Customer discloses five mini-split heat pumps, a strong usage signal that supports a larger system design and justifies bill savings even on a modest $100-120 bill.
coaching_implication: Rep should have reflected this back ('five mini splits means your usage is probably higher than the bill number alone suggests') to build the case for solar rather than noting 'not the highest bill' at 03:43.

quote: Not, like, the highest bill, but I think we can definitely still save you some money.
stewart_read: Rep files the $100-120 bill and states a vague savings claim instead of flipping it into an emotional hook (e.g., contrasting it against a brand-new home's expected usage or the mini splits).
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive: rep treats a modest bill as a mild deflator rather than using the enthusiasm signal (mini splits) to reframe upward.
coaching_implication: Use ancillary usage signals (mini splits, new construction) to reframe a modest bill as still worth solving instead of undercutting the pitch with 'not the highest bill.'

quote: I'll need two things from you. Just the the drone shot, if you could get a hold of that.
stewart_read: Rep sets a real barrier (drone shot + bill) as a gate to scheduling, but never resolves either live on the call.
coaching_implication: Should have attempted verbal bill read-back live per bill_collection.alternative_paths instead of deferring both documents to an after-call text.

quote: I would need the the picture of the roof and then the utility bill before I can put you in the schedule.
stewart_read: Second touch on the same unresolved gate — rep restates the same requirement instead of resolving it before locking the appointment.
coaching_implication: This is the moment to try live capture (verbal kWh readback) rather than deferring again; repeating the requirement without resolving it weakens the booking.

quote: Carter. Alright, Carter. I'll see and you'll be visiting the house tomorrow?
stewart_read: Customer's own confusion about who is visiting reveals the button-up never clearly separated 'specialist visit' from 'setter call' and never got an explicit 'is that fair?' handshake.
coaching_implication: Run the full button-up: confirm date/time, one-hour block, phone vs in-person format, and the fairness handshake explicitly so the customer doesn't have to ask who's coming.
